newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere, Alcatel eager for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere, Alcatel eager for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: The Lagardere group said on Wednesday it was ready to adapt to the new setting since the election of a Socialist-led French government and would continue to pursue a linkup with defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
"We think that the Thomson-Matra merger remains the only answer to the dynamism of the Americans," Matra High Technology chairman Noel Forgeard told reporters at the Paris air show.

"We have to respond by regrouping. Will the merger between Thomson-CSF and Matra be done on the same terms? I cannot say. The rules will be set, we will adapt to them," he said. Matra is a subsidiary of Lagardere.
Lagardere is bidding against telecommunications group Alcatel Alsthom in the sale of the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF launched by the previous conservative government.
But industry executives are eagerly awaiting policy announcements by the new government, which showed its hostility to sell-offs during the election campaign.
"We are certain that the European approach that we have chosen is the right one," Forgeard said.
Lagardere has allied itself with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) of Germany and British Aerospace Plc in its bid.
Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk told a later news conference that his company's bid still remained valid.

"Our plan has not lost any of its industrial qualities, there is no reason for it to lose them," he told reporters. I have not changed my opinion on Thomson. I think the industrial plan should be the guide for the transaction.
"We have honestly formulated what I believe to be an excellent industrial plan with Thomson, Aerospatiale and Dassault," he said.

"I put the priority on the industrial plan and the industrial consequences of the options that we are taking. And we will see if the government's choice match with the industrial plan that we have drawn up," he added.
Alcatel joined with privately-owned Dassault Industries for its bid and has assigned a large role for joint ventures with state-owned Aerospatiale in its business plan for Thomson-CSF.
The government ruled out Aerospatiale from making its own bid as it is state-owned.
